extracted.intended_audience: prospective applicants to the Knight-Hennessy Scholars program (applicants to Stanford graduate programs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for applying to the Knight-Hennessy Scholars (KHS) program alongside Stanford graduate degree program applications, covering eligibility, materials, evaluation process, and finalist requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum degree equivalency for eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for graduate study at Stanford University, you must meet the requirements of the graduate program(s) that you wish to pursue and hold the equivalent of a U.S. bachelor's degree from a college or university of recognized standing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Stanford's guidelines for minimum level of study for international applicants. (The Office of Graduate Admissions, not Knight-Hennessy Scholars, sets these policies.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Seven-year rule from first/bachelor's degree
rubrics_metrics.description: If you earned your first/bachelor's degree more than seven years before your intended enrollment date, then you are not eligible for consideration as a Knight-Hennessy scholar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies even if you have earned an additional degree later. Example: for autumn 2027 intake, degrees earned in 2019 or earlier are ineligible. Those who served in their country's military have two additional years of eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undocumented/DACA eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who have been granted DACA status, do not hold formal citizenship in any country, or are otherwise undocumented are eligible to apply for graduate study and matriculate at Stanford University and Knight-Hennessy Scholars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For more information, refer to the Undocumented at Stanford website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility with an existing graduate degree
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have earned a graduate degree, you remain eligible to enroll as a Knight-Hennessy scholar as long as you earned your first/bachelor's degree within the 7-year eligibility window (or with military extension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The seven-year rule is tied to the first/bachelor's degree date, not subsequent graduate degrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current Stanford graduate enrollment timing restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Stanford PhD students who will start their PhD in 2026 may apply to KHS in 2026 to start KHS in 2027 (their second year of PhD enrollment). Otherwise, if you enrolled in a graduate degree program at Stanford in 2025 or earlier, you are not eligible for consideration as a Knight-Hennessy scholar for your current degree program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you intend to apply to an additional degree program at Stanford, review the related FAQ about applying while enrolled and deferring enrollment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applying while deferring or changing Stanford enrollment
rubrics_metrics.description: You may apply to Knight-Hennessy Scholars if you defer enrollment to 2027, or if you apply for a new graduate degree program at Stanford that starts in 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: If admitted to Stanford MBA and deferred to Sept 2027, you may apply to KHS in 2026 to enroll as a scholar in 2027, aligning graduate program and KHS enrollment years.

rubrics_metrics.name: KHS offers are not deferrable
rubrics_metrics.description: Knight-Hennessy Scholars does not defer scholar offers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If selected and unable to enroll, you must reapply for the year you intend to enroll. Deferral of enrollment to a graduate program is handled by that department, not KHS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with other fellowships/awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Some fellowships administered at Stanford may or may not be combined with KHS; applicants should confirm eligibility based on a provided list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards marked 'No' may not be combined with KHS and may not be discontinued in order to apply to KHS. (Example list includes ARCS: Yes; CCSRE: No; Dissertation Completion Fellowship: Yes; Gerald J. Lieberman Fellowship: Yes; RAISE: Yes; SGF: Yes; Shoucheng Zhang Graduate Fellowship: No; SIGF: Yes.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctness of KHS and Stanford degree applications
rubrics_metrics.description: While some content may overlap across applications (transcripts, resume), you are encouraged to approach each application distinctly and tailor essays/personal statements to their specific prompts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may choose the same recommenders for both applications but should encourage them to tailor letters for each. Check degree program websites for additional materials KHS does not require.

rubrics_metrics.name: KHS review does not replace graduate program review
rubrics_metrics.description: Knight-Hennessy Scholars does not review your Stanford degree program(s) application(s) or associated documents; separate admission committees handle degree program admissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application materials are not customarily shared between KHS and degree program committees except in rare cases. KHS checks with departments at intervals to verify applicant submission and competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-submission edits allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Once you submit your KHS application you cannot edit it except for specific permitted changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted edits via the Application Status page: Adding test scores, Changing recommenders, Changing your intended Stanford graduate degree program(s), Uploading an updated resume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application fee and fee waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no application fee for Knight-Hennessy Scholars; however, degree program application fees (if any) must be paid by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KHS cannot provide fee waivers for degree program applications; review Graduate Admissions for fee/waiver information.

rubrics_metrics.name: COVID-19 grading (pass/fail) consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: KHS recognizes institutional changes to grading policy due to COVID-19 and will not penalize applicants for an institutional change that was out of the applicant's control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications will be reviewed contextually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-English transcripts requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Transcripts and degree documents that are in a language other than English must be accompanied by an official English translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: No minimum GPA/test score requirement for KHS
rubrics_metrics.description: Although KHS expects scholars to have performed well, there is no minimum requirement for grades or test scores for KHS consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must meet any minimums set by the graduate degree program to which they are applying. Consult the degree program website for its admission requirements and minimums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling tests unavailable by KHS deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: If you will not have test scores until after the KHS application deadline, you may leave the test scores section blank when submitting and provide scores later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide scores when available via your Application Status page. If you recently sat for an exam that provides unofficial scores immediately, you may report those.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updating test scores after submission
rubrics_metrics.description: You may update your test score after submitting your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit updates via the Test Score Update form on your status page after submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting test scores for multiple degree programs
rubrics_metrics.description: If applying to multiple Stanford graduate degree programs, you must submit required test scores for each of those programs to Knight-Hennessy Scholars.

rubrics_metrics.name: English proficiency test submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Stanford graduate degree program requires English proficiency test results, you must submit them to KHS as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All Stanford graduate programs accept TOEFL. Most accept IELTS. MBA also accepts PTE. Some departments accept scores from the last 18 months; others 24 months. Check the intended degree program website for accepted tests and recency requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: English proficiency minimums
rubrics_metrics.description: KHS does not set minimum English test scores, but applicants must meet the minimums required by their graduate degree program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For most programs, typical admission consideration minimums are TOEFL 90 and IELTS 7; verify with the specific program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation letter guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommenders: You may ask the same person to provide recommendations for both KHS and your graduate degree program(s), but letters should be tailored to each application. Family members should not write recommendations; peers are acceptable if they are not 'friends' but collaborators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a work email address for recommenders when available. KHS typically reviews only the recommendation letters submitted specifically for KHS, though it may occasionally request program letters if helpful. Do not delay submitting your application because recommenders have not yet submitted letters; submit your portion by the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short answer and essay guidance — 'improbable facts'
rubrics_metrics.description: Improbable facts are aspects about you (experiences, beliefs, traits, skills, etc.) that seem unlikely but are true; these can show a different side of you and are not a list of achievements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to show a different side of yourself and have some fun.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short Answer 2 structure flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: For Short Answer 2 (three-part prompt about engaging with different perspective, acting with courage, falling short of expectations), you do not need to use one example to address all three parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may respond with one integrated example or address each part with separate examples. Structure your response in the way that most clearly and authentically conveys your experiences and reflections within the 250-word limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: KHS and degree program application completion requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You must complete both your Knight-Hennessy Scholars application AND the entire application process for your graduate degree program(s), including any required standardized tests and English proficiency tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degree program applications may require a fee. Visit the graduate program(s) for specific requirements and admission process details.

rubrics_metrics.name: KHS selection contingent on graduate program admission
rubrics_metrics.description: You must receive an offer of admission from a Stanford graduate degree program in order to be a Knight-Hennessy scholar; KHS cannot admit you to Stanford independently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KHS checks with graduate programs regularly to verify which KHS applicants have applied and remain competitive. Only applicants whom the degree program verifies as eligible will be advanced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission outcomes can differ between KHS and degree program
rubrics_metrics.description: It is possible to be admitted to the Stanford degree program but not selected for KHS, and vice versa in terms of timing; receiving one decision does not guarantee the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many applicants admitted to their degree program but not KHS still enroll at Stanford. Apply to KHS confidently; KHS application does not preclude admission to Stanford.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video statement content and role
rubrics_metrics.description: The video prompt is intentionally broad and does not have to be about something academic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finalist selection is based on the application, the video statement, and verification that you remain competitive for admission to your Stanford graduate program; the video alone is not the sole basis for selection. Video invitations are sent on a rolling basis in January.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immersion Weekend attendance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Barring unforeseen circumstances and/or immediate family obligations, you must attend Immersion Weekend to be considered for selection to Knight-Hennessy Scholars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a conflict during Immersion Weekend dates, absence may affect consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visa invitation letters for finalists
rubrics_metrics.description: If you need a visa to visit the U.S., KHS will work with selected finalists to coordinate a visa invitation letter as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KHS cannot provide letters of invitation before finalists are selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview timing for finalists
rubrics_metrics.description: KHS interviews take place only during designated time periods for finalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may not interview for KHS at arbitrary times (for example, concurrently with a degree program interview) — interviews are scheduled for finalists only.
